articles.excerpt: If you have ever needed to export a multi-sheet .xlsx spreadsheet with formatted currency headers and live formulas (SUM, ROUND, IFERROR) from a lightweight Node.js script, pulling in a multi-megabyte…
articles.body: If you have ever needed to export a multi-sheet .xlsx spreadsheet with formatted currency headers and live formulas ( SUM , ROUND , IFERROR ) from a lightweight Node.js script, pulling in a multi-megabyte dependency chain just to write four worksheets feels excessive. Under the hood, an .xlsx file is just a standard ZIP archive containing a small handful of UTF-8 XML files conforming to ECMA-376 OpenXML. Once you know the three strict invariants Microsoft Excel and LibreOffice Calc expect, you can emit rock-solid workbooks in ~150 lines of Node.js with zero npm spreadsheet dependencies. Here are the exact implementation details we used to build the 4-tab OpenXML workbook inside Lark Dev Vault . 1.

articles.excerpt: Exploring self-evolving AI agents, self-adapting language models, and the possibility of an intelligence explosion. For decades, humans have been the architects of artificial intelligence. We design n…
articles.body: Exploring self-evolving AI agents, self-adapting language models, and the possibility of an intelligence explosion. For decades, humans have been the architects of artificial intelligence. We design neural networks, develop training algorithms, prepare datasets, evaluate performance, and build increasingly capable models. But what happens when AI itself becomes an active participant in this process? What if future generations of AI are designed not just by human researchers, but also by previous generations of AI? What if an AI system could discover better algorithms, improve its own capabilities, and then use those improved capabilities to improve itself even further?

Instead, I decided to run an experiment: could ChatGPT, running GPT-6, design the same part from a natural-language description and manufacturer documentation? The answer was yes — eventually. We got a working part, but it took approximately three hours of active interaction with AI. Most of that time wasn't spent modeling anything. articles.title: 8 Classic PlayStation Games That Are Barely Playable Today
articles.excerpt: From Tomb Raider to Silent Hill, eight classic PlayStation games whose tank controls, cameras, or lost code make them hard to play today
articles.body: If you’ve ever watched someone play an old PlayStation game and wondered why their character keeps spinning around in circles, congratulations, you’ve already met tank controls. If you’re unfamiliar, here’s your quick introduction: With tank controls, pressing up moves your character forward in whatever direction they’re facing, and pressing left or right only rotates them, so with the stick alone, you can’t sidestep or turn on a dime. That’s manageable in a hallway. It’s much less so when you’re sneaking past a guard, lining up a shot, or timing a leap across a pit, which is why the same scheme caused trouble in just about every genre during the PS1 era. These eight classic games are the hardest to go back to, whether the culprit is tank controls or something else entirely.

Atmos, a space company known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle , will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project. "We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, said in a statement on Nov. 18. The system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies said that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration.
